experiment: E2 -- in-process defender subversion vs an external observer
substrate: real deployment (mosquitto broker, MQTT discovery, shipped blueprint)

hook.mechanism: a second community integration rebinds homeprov._graph

in_process_defender.note: the defender sees one row fewer than exists; the missing row is the adversary's own

adversary_rows_in_recorder.note: the minted context owned the call_service event; no state row carried it

external_monitor.placement: separate container, /config mounted read-only, unreachable by the in-process rebinding

finding: The in-process defender was blinded to the adversary's row by a rebinding that cost the adversary nothing but an import. The external monitor sealed the exact second that row fell in, with n=1. A defender sharing the interpreter cannot carry the guarantee; one outside it can.
not_shown: the deletion step (removing the censored rows so the database matches the defender's view) was not performed in this run, so this artifact does not evidence an anchor segment surviving a database the rows no longer support; that remains evidenced only by the earlier run in results/bundles/u_res_e2.json
caveat: the in-hub homeprov component's own anchoring was erroring throughout (/anchor/chain not present in its container), so this run evidences the EXTERNAL monitor's behaviour and the blinding of the in-process view, not the in-process anchor's silence
